cards.definition: A return to an earlier working version after a change causes problems.
cards.turkishMeaning: Önceki çalışan sürüme geri dönüş.
examples: The **rollback** restored the previous release.
We need a **rollback** plan before deployment.
cards.note: The noun is rollback; the verb is roll back.

cards.definition: Preparing and supplying the resources a system needs.
cards.turkishMeaning: Kaynakları hazırlama ve kullanıma sunma.
examples: Automated **provisioning** saves us time.
Server **provisioning** takes five minutes.
cards.note: More than buying hardware: it includes configuring resources.

cards.definition: Producing the same final effect when repeated as when done once.
cards.turkishMeaning: Tekrarlansa da aynı nihai etkiyi oluşturan.
examples: This **idempotent** operation can be retried safely.
Make the setup script **idempotent**.
cards.note: The final effect is stable; responses may still differ.

cards.definition: Available to respond to urgent work problems outside normal duties.
cards.turkishMeaning: Gerektiğinde müdahale etmek üzere nöbetçi.
examples: The **on-call** engineer received an alert.
Check the **on-call** schedule before the weekend.
cards.note: Hyphenated before a noun; you can also say I am on call.

cards.definition: A review after an incident to understand causes and improve systems.
cards.turkishMeaning: Olay sonrası neden ve iyileştirme değerlendirmesi.
examples: We held a **post-mortem** after the outage.
The **post-mortem** lists three follow-up actions.
cards.note: In engineering, aim for a blameless review.

cards.definition: Putting a software version into an environment where it can run.
cards.turkishMeaning: Yazılımı çalışacağı ortama dağıtma.
examples: The **deployment** finished without errors.
We paused the **deployment** during the incident.
cards.note: Deployment and release can be separate steps.

cards.definition: How reliably a service is ready for people to use.
cards.turkishMeaning: Bir hizmetin kullanılabilir olma durumu.
examples: We measure **availability** every month.
The team improved **availability** by removing a single point of failure.
cards.note: Usually uncountable in this meaning.

cards.definition: The delay before a request receives a response.
cards.turkishMeaning: İstek ile yanıt arasındaki gecikme.
examples: Network **latency** increased this morning.
We reduced **latency** by caching common results.
cards.note: Low latency means a shorter delay.

cards.definition: The amount of work a system completes in a period of time.
cards.turkishMeaning: Bir sistemin birim zamanda işlediği iş miktarı.
examples: The queue's **throughput** doubled after the change.
We measure **throughput** in requests per second.
cards.note: Not the same as latency: rate versus delay.

cards.definition: A part of a system that limits overall speed or capacity.
cards.turkishMeaning: Darboğaz.
examples: The database became a **bottleneck**.
Profiling helped us find the **bottleneck**.
cards.note: Also used for slow steps in a work process.

cards.definition: The ability to handle more work by increasing resources.
cards.turkishMeaning: Artan yükü kaynak ekleyerek karşılayabilme yeteneği.
examples: We tested the service's **scalability**.
Good **scalability** matters during traffic spikes.
cards.note: Distinguish from availability: capacity growth versus readiness.

cards.definition: A component that distributes incoming traffic across servers.
cards.turkishMeaning: Gelen trafiği sunuculara dağıtan bileşen.
examples: The **load balancer** routes requests to healthy servers.
We placed a **load balancer** in front of the application.
cards.note: Two words; balancer is a countable noun.

cards.definition: A test that checks whether a service is working well enough to use.
cards.turkishMeaning: Bir hizmetin çalışır durumda olup olmadığını denetleyen test.
examples: The **health check** failed after the restart.
Add a **health check** to the container.
cards.note: A passing check only confirms the conditions it tests.

cards.definition: Switching to a backup system when the primary system fails.
cards.turkishMeaning: Ana sistem arızalandığında yedek sisteme geçiş.
examples: Automatic **failover** restored the service.
We tested **failover** in a staging environment.
cards.note: Noun: failover. Verb: fail over.

cards.definition: Managing infrastructure through versioned machine-readable definitions.
cards.turkishMeaning: Altyapıyı sürümlenen kod tanımlarıyla yönetme.
examples: We use **infrastructure as code** to manage our environments.
**Infrastructure as code** makes changes easier to review.
cards.note: Often abbreviated to IaC.

cards.definition: Giving only the access needed to perform a task.
cards.turkishMeaning: Yalnızca görev için gereken en az yetkiyi verme ilkesi.
examples: This role follows the principle of **least privilege**.
We applied **least privilege** to the service account.
cards.note: Privilege refers to permission here.

cards.definition: Sensitive data such as a password, token, or private key.
cards.turkishMeaning: Parola, belirteç veya özel anahtar gibi hassas veri.
examples: Never commit a **secret** to the repository.
Rotate the **secret** after a suspected leak.
cards.note: A secret is sensitive even when stored in an environment variable.

cards.definition: A proposal to review and merge changes into a codebase.
cards.turkishMeaning: Kod değişikliklerini inceleme ve birleştirme önerisi.
examples: Could you review my **pull request**?
This **pull request** fixes the timeout.
cards.note: Commonly shortened to PR.

cards.term: Could you take a look at
cards.definition: Used to ask someone to examine something.
cards.turkishMeaning: … bir göz atabilir misin?
examples: **Could you take a look at** my pull request?
**Could you take a look at** these logs?
cards.note: Give context and say what kind of feedback you need.

cards.definition: I cannot continue because of a specific obstacle.
cards.turkishMeaning: … nedeniyle ilerleyemiyorum.
examples: **I'm blocked by** a missing permission.
**I'm blocked by** the failing integration test.
cards.note: Useful in stand-ups; name the obstacle clearly.

cards.definition: Check progress or take further action about something.
cards.turkishMeaning: Bir konunun takibini yapmak.
examples: I'll **follow up on** the support ticket.
Can you **follow up on** yesterday's action items?
cards.note: Verb: follow up. Noun/adjective: follow-up.

cards.definition: Continue giving you updates.
cards.turkishMeaning: Seni gelişmelerden haberdar etmek.
examples: I'll **keep you posted** on the investigation.
We will **keep you posted** as we learn more.
cards.note: Useful during incidents; add a specific next update time.

cards.definition: An underlying reason that a problem happened.
cards.turkishMeaning: Bir sorunun temel nedeni.
examples: We are still investigating the **root cause**.
The report explains one **root cause** of the failure.
cards.note: Complex incidents may have several contributing causes.

cards.definition: A temporary way to avoid a problem without fully fixing it.
cards.turkishMeaning: Kalıcı çözüm yerine kullanılan geçici yöntem.
examples: Restarting the worker is a temporary **workaround**.
We documented the **workaround** for support.
cards.note: One word as a noun; work around is a verb phrase.

cards.definition: A choice that gains one benefit while giving up another.
cards.turkishMeaning: Bir avantaj için başka bir avantajdan ödün verme.
examples: There is a **trade-off** between cost and speed.
Explain the **trade-off** in your design proposal.
cards.note: Also written tradeoff, especially in American English.

cards.definition: Able to work with older versions or existing users of an interface.
cards.turkishMeaning: Önceki sürümlerle uyumlu.
examples: The new API is **backward compatible**.
We must keep the file format **backward compatible**.
cards.note: Before a noun, use a hyphen: a backward-compatible change.

cards.definition: Mark a feature as discouraged and potentially removable later.
cards.turkishMeaning: Bir özelliğin kullanımını artık önermemek ve kaldırılabileceğini belirtmek.
examples: We plan to **deprecate** the old endpoint.
Do not **deprecate** this option without a migration guide.
cards.note: Deprecated does not necessarily mean removed or broken.

cards.definition: Conditions that must be met for work to be accepted.
cards.turkishMeaning: İşin kabul edilmesi için karşılanması gereken koşullar.
examples: The ticket needs clear **acceptance criteria**.
We checked the **acceptance criteria** before closing the task.
cards.note: Criteria is plural; the singular is criterion.

cards.definition: Used to ask someone to explain something more clearly.
cards.turkishMeaning: … açıklığa kavuşturabilir misiniz?
examples: **Could you clarify** the expected behavior?
**Could you clarify** which environment is affected?
cards.note: Ask a specific question to avoid ambiguity.

cards.definition: Used to introduce experience from an earlier job.
cards.turkishMeaning: Önceki görevimde.
examples: **In my previous role**, I maintained deployment pipelines.
**In my previous role**, I helped reduce incident response time.
cards.note: In interviews, follow with a concrete action and result.

cards.definition: A packaged environment that runs an application with its dependencies.
cards.turkishMeaning: Uygulamayı bağımlılıklarıyla çalıştıran paketlenmiş ortam.
examples: The **container** starts in a few seconds.
We run the worker inside a **container**.

cards.definition: A template used to create a container or machine.
cards.turkishMeaning: Konteyner veya makine oluşturmak için kullanılan kalıp.
examples: Build the **image** before deployment.
The **image** contains the application and its libraries.

cards.definition: A service that stores and distributes software images or packages.
cards.turkishMeaning: Yazılım imajlarını veya paketlerini saklayıp dağıtan hizmet.
examples: Push the image to the **registry**.
Our private **registry** requires authentication.

cards.definition: A group of computers working together.
cards.turkishMeaning: Birlikte çalışan bilgisayar grubu.
examples: The **cluster** has three nodes.
We added capacity to the **cluster**.

cards.definition: One machine or participant in a distributed system.
cards.turkishMeaning: Dağıtık sistemdeki tek makine veya katılımcı.
examples: This **node** is running out of memory.
The scheduler selected a healthy **node**.

cards.definition: A Kubernetes unit containing one or more closely related containers.
cards.turkishMeaning: Kubernetes'te bir veya daha fazla ilişkili konteyner içeren birim.
examples: The **pod** contains the app and a sidecar.
Check the events when a **pod** cannot start.

cards.definition: A named scope used to organize and separate resources.
cards.turkishMeaning: Kaynakları düzenlemek ve ayırmak için adlandırılmış kapsam.
examples: Create a **namespace** for the test environment.
The service lives in a different **namespace**.

cards.definition: A copy of a running workload or stored data.
cards.turkishMeaning: Çalışan iş yükünün veya verinin kopyası.
examples: One **replica** is still starting.
The database keeps a **replica** in another zone.

cards.definition: A file describing the intended configuration of a resource.
cards.turkishMeaning: Bir kaynağın istenen yapılandırmasını tanımlayan dosya.
examples: Review the **manifest** before applying it.
The **manifest** declares two replicas.

cards.definition: Incoming traffic or a rule controlling traffic entering a system.
cards.turkishMeaning: Sisteme giren trafik veya bunu yöneten kural.
examples: The **ingress** rule routes traffic by hostname.
Check **ingress** settings if the site is unreachable.

cards.definition: Traffic leaving a network or service.
cards.turkishMeaning: Ağdan veya hizmetten çıkan trafik.
examples: We restrict **egress** to approved destinations.
Cross-region **egress** can increase costs.

cards.definition: Finding the network location of a service automatically.
cards.turkishMeaning: Bir hizmetin ağ konumunu otomatik bulma.
examples: DNS supports our **service discovery**.
Broken **service discovery** prevents workers from connecting.

cards.definition: A specific address through which a service can be accessed.
cards.turkishMeaning: Bir hizmete erişilen belirli adres.
examples: This **endpoint** returns account details.
The health **endpoint** does not require a login.

cards.definition: A system that filters network traffic using rules.
cards.turkishMeaning: Kurallarla ağ trafiğini süzen sistem.
examples: The **firewall** blocks incoming connections.
Add a narrow rule to the **firewall**.

cards.definition: A smaller logical network within a larger network.
cards.turkishMeaning: Daha büyük bir ağ içindeki alt ağ.
examples: Place the database in a private **subnet**.
Each zone uses a separate **subnet**.

cards.definition: Choosing where network traffic should go.
cards.turkishMeaning: Ağ trafiğinin gideceği yolu seçme.
examples: The **routing** table contains a default route.
Incorrect **routing** caused the connection failure.

cards.definition: A readable name used to locate an internet resource.
cards.turkishMeaning: İnternet kaynağını bulmak için kullanılan okunabilir ad.
examples: We registered a new **domain name**.
Point the **domain name** to the load balancer.

cards.definition: A digital document used to verify identity and support secure connections.
cards.turkishMeaning: Kimliği doğrulayan ve güvenli bağlantıyı destekleyen dijital belge.
examples: The TLS **certificate** expires next month.
Renew the **certificate** before it becomes invalid.

cards.definition: Transforming data so that only authorized parties can read it.
cards.turkishMeaning: Veriyi yalnızca yetkililerin okuyabileceği biçime dönüştürme.
examples: Enable **encryption** for stored backups.
TLS provides **encryption** in transit.

cards.definition: Checking who a user or system is.
cards.turkishMeaning: Kullanıcı veya sistem kimliğini doğrulama.
examples: The service requires **authentication**.
Failed **authentication** should return a clear error.

cards.definition: Deciding what an identified user or system may do.
cards.turkishMeaning: Kimliği bilinen kişinin veya sistemin yetkilerini belirleme.
examples: The **authorization** check denied the request.
Keep **authorization** separate from login logic.

cards.definition: An identity used by software rather than a person.
cards.turkishMeaning: İnsan yerine yazılım tarafından kullanılan kimlik.
examples: The job runs under a **service account**.
Give the **service account** only the required permissions.

cards.definition: Rules describing which actions an identity may perform.
cards.turkishMeaning: Bir kimliğin yapabileceği işlemleri tanımlayan kurallar.
examples: Review the **access policy** before granting permissions.
This **access policy** allows read-only access.

cards.definition: A record of actions used to investigate access and changes.
cards.turkishMeaning: Erişim ve değişiklikleri incelemek için tutulan işlem kaydı.
examples: The **audit log** shows who changed the policy.
Store the **audit log** in a protected location.

cards.definition: A weakness that could be used to compromise a system.
cards.turkishMeaning: Sistemin güvenliğini tehlikeye atabilecek zayıflık.
examples: The scanner found a critical **vulnerability**.
Patch the **vulnerability** in the base image.

cards.definition: A small software update that fixes a problem.
cards.turkishMeaning: Sorunu gideren küçük yazılım güncellemesi.
examples: Apply the security **patch** tonight.
The **patch** fixes a memory leak.

cards.definition: A component another component needs to work.
cards.turkishMeaning: Başka bir bileşenin çalışmak için ihtiyaç duyduğu bileşen.
examples: We upgraded the database **dependency**.
A missing **dependency** caused the build to fail.

cards.definition: A file produced by a build or other automated process.
cards.turkishMeaning: Derleme veya otomasyon sonucunda üretilen dosya.
examples: Upload the build **artifact** after the tests pass.
The release **artifact** includes the executable.

cards.definition: A sequence of automated steps that process code or data.
cards.turkishMeaning: Kod veya veriyi işleyen otomatik adımlar dizisi.
examples: The **pipeline** runs tests before deployment.
Our delivery **pipeline** stopped at the approval step.

cards.definition: The process or result of turning source code into runnable software.
cards.turkishMeaning: Kaynak kodu çalışabilir yazılıma dönüştürme işlemi veya çıktısı.
examples: The **build** failed because of a syntax error.
Download the latest successful **build**.

cards.definition: A version of software made available to users.
cards.turkishMeaning: Kullanıcılara sunulan yazılım sürümü.
examples: This **release** adds dark mode.
We delayed the **release** to fix a bug.

cards.definition: An environment used to test changes before production.
cards.turkishMeaning: Canlıya çıkmadan önce değişiklikleri sınayan ortam.
examples: Deploy the change to **staging** first.
The issue also occurs in **staging**.

cards.definition: The live environment used by real customers.
cards.turkishMeaning: Gerçek kullanıcıların kullandığı canlı ortam.
examples: The fix is now in **production**.
Avoid testing destructive changes in **production**.

cards.definition: An isolated environment for safer experimentation.
cards.turkishMeaning: Daha güvenli denemeler için yalıtılmış ortam.
examples: Try the script in a **sandbox**.
The **sandbox** has no production credentials.

cards.definition: A difference between actual and intended configuration over time.
cards.turkishMeaning: Gerçek ve amaçlanan yapılandırmanın zamanla farklılaşması.
examples: Manual changes caused **configuration drift**.
Our nightly check detects **configuration drift**.

cards.definition: A file recording the resources managed by an infrastructure tool.
cards.turkishMeaning: Altyapı aracının yönettiği kaynakları kaydeden dosya.
examples: Protect the **state file** because it may contain sensitive data.
Use locking when updating the **state file**.

cards.definition: Not changed after creation.
cards.turkishMeaning: Oluşturulduktan sonra değiştirilmeyen.
examples: We deploy **immutable** images.
An **immutable** object cannot be modified in place.

cards.definition: Able to be repeated with the same result.
cards.turkishMeaning: Aynı sonuçla yeniden üretilebilen.
examples: We need a **reproducible** test case.
Pin dependencies to make builds more **reproducible**.

cards.definition: Able to keep working or recover after a failure.
cards.turkishMeaning: Arıza karşısında çalışmayı sürdürebilen veya toparlanabilen.
examples: A **resilient** service handles temporary failures.
We designed a more **resilient** messaging system.

cards.definition: Able to continue operating when some components fail.
cards.turkishMeaning: Bazı bileşenler arızalansa da çalışabilen.
examples: The storage system is **fault tolerant**.
Redundancy helps make the service **fault tolerant**.

cards.definition: Extra components that can take over if others fail.
cards.turkishMeaning: Arızalarda devreye girebilen yedek bileşenler.
examples: We added **redundancy** across two zones.
Without **redundancy**, one failed server can stop the service.

cards.definition: One component whose failure can stop the whole system.
cards.turkishMeaning: Arızası tüm sistemi durdurabilecek tek bileşen.
examples: The shared database is a **single point of failure**.
Remove this **single point of failure** before launch.

cards.definition: A separate copy of data kept for recovery.
cards.turkishMeaning: Kurtarma amacıyla tutulan ayrı veri kopyası.
examples: Test the **backup** by restoring it.
We create a **backup** every night.

cards.definition: Bring data or a system back from a saved copy.
cards.turkishMeaning: Veriyi veya sistemi kaydedilmiş kopyadan geri yüklemek.
examples: We can **restore** the database from yesterday's backup.
How long does it take to **restore** the service?

cards.definition: Plans and procedures for recovering from a major outage.
cards.turkishMeaning: Büyük kesintiden kurtulma plan ve süreçleri.
examples: Test the **disaster recovery** plan regularly.
Our **disaster recovery** exercise revealed a missing dependency.

cards.definition: The target maximum time to restore a service.
cards.turkishMeaning: Hizmeti geri getirmek için hedeflenen azami süre.
examples: Our **recovery time objective** is one hour.
The **recovery time objective** guides the recovery plan.

cards.definition: The maximum acceptable age of data lost during recovery.
cards.turkishMeaning: Kurtarmada kaybedilmesi kabul edilen verinin azami yaş aralığı.
examples: The **recovery point objective** is fifteen minutes.
Frequent backups help meet the **recovery point objective**.

cards.definition: Time during which a system is operating.
cards.turkishMeaning: Sistemin çalışır durumda olduğu süre.
examples: The dashboard reports service **uptime**.
Maintenance may reduce measured **uptime**.

cards.definition: Time during which a service is unavailable.
cards.turkishMeaning: Hizmetin kullanılamadığı süre.
examples: The outage caused ten minutes of **downtime**.
We aim to deploy without **downtime**.

cards.definition: An event that disrupts or threatens normal service.
cards.turkishMeaning: Normal hizmeti bozan veya tehdit eden olay.
examples: We opened an **incident** after the error rate increased.
Assign an owner to the **incident**.

cards.definition: A period when a service is not available.
cards.turkishMeaning: Hizmet kesintisi.
examples: The **outage** affected one region.
We published a summary of the **outage**.

cards.definition: A measure of how serious a problem is.
cards.turkishMeaning: Sorunun ne kadar ciddi olduğunu belirten ölçü.
examples: Set the incident **severity** based on user impact.
The team lowered the **severity** after recovery.

cards.definition: Sending an issue to someone with more expertise or authority.
cards.turkishMeaning: Sorunu daha yetkili veya uzman kişiye aktarma.
examples: The alert triggered an **escalation**.
Follow the **escalation** policy if nobody responds.

cards.definition: An action that reduces the impact of a problem.
cards.turkishMeaning: Sorunun etkisini azaltan önlem.
examples: Rate limiting was our first **mitigation**.
The **mitigation** restored most requests.

cards.definition: Work that fixes the underlying problem.
cards.turkishMeaning: Temel sorunu gideren düzeltici çalışma.
examples: The team scheduled permanent **remediation**.
Track the **remediation** tasks after the incident.

cards.definition: Written steps for performing an operational task.
cards.turkishMeaning: Operasyonel görevin yazılı uygulama adımları.
examples: Follow the **runbook** to restart the service.
Update the **runbook** after discovering a missing step.

cards.definition: A guide describing actions for a particular situation.
cards.turkishMeaning: Belirli durum için yapılacakları anlatan rehber.
examples: The incident **playbook** defines communication roles.
Use the **playbook** during the exercise.

cards.definition: A notification that a condition needs attention.
cards.turkishMeaning: İlgilenilmesi gereken durumu bildiren uyarı.
examples: The **alert** fired when latency increased.
This **alert** has a link to the runbook.

cards.definition: A limit that triggers an action when crossed.
cards.turkishMeaning: Aşıldığında işlem başlatan eşik.
examples: The error rate exceeded the **threshold**.
Adjust the **threshold** to reduce false alarms.

cards.definition: An alert or result that incorrectly reports a problem.
cards.turkishMeaning: Olmayan sorunu var gösteren sonuç.
examples: The security alert was a **false positive**.
We tuned the rule after another **false positive**.

cards.definition: The ability to understand internal system behavior from its outputs.
cards.turkishMeaning: Sistem davranışını ürettiği verilerden anlayabilme.
examples: Better **observability** shortened the investigation.
Logs, metrics, and traces support **observability**.

cards.definition: A numerical measurement of a system.
cards.turkishMeaning: Sisteme ait sayısal ölçüm.
examples: This **metric** tracks failed requests.
Choose a **metric** that reflects user experience.

cards.definition: A record of one request's path through a system.
cards.turkishMeaning: Bir isteğin sistemde izlediği yolun kaydı.
examples: The **trace** shows a slow database call.
Use the request ID to find the **trace**.

cards.definition: One timed operation within a distributed trace.
cards.turkishMeaning: Dağıtık iz içindeki süreli tek işlem.
examples: This **span** represents the database query.
The parent **span** includes two child operations.

cards.definition: Collecting logs from many sources in one place.
cards.turkishMeaning: Birçok kaynaktan günlükleri tek yerde toplama.
examples: Centralized **log aggregation** helps investigations.
Our **log aggregation** service receives container output.

cards.definition: A measurable target for service reliability.
cards.turkishMeaning: Hizmet güvenilirliği için ölçülebilir hedef.
examples: The **service level objective** covers successful requests.
Review the **service level objective** with the product team.

cards.definition: The amount of unreliability allowed by a service objective.
cards.turkishMeaning: Hizmet hedefinin izin verdiği güvenilirlik kaybı payı.
examples: We used most of the **error budget** this month.
A depleted **error budget** can pause risky releases.

cards.definition: Restricting how many requests may be made in a period.
cards.turkishMeaning: Belirli sürede yapılabilecek istek sayısını sınırlama.
examples: Enable **rate limiting** on public endpoints.
The client must handle responses from **rate limiting**.

cards.definition: Reducing or restricting the rate of work.
cards.turkishMeaning: İşlem hızını azaltma veya sınırlama.
examples: CPU **throttling** slowed the container.
The API uses **throttling** to protect shared resources.

cards.definition: An additional attempt after a failure.
cards.turkishMeaning: Başarısızlık sonrası yeniden deneme.
examples: A **retry** may succeed after a temporary error.
Limit the number of **retry** attempts.

cards.definition: Increasing the delay between repeated attempts by a multiplying factor.
cards.turkishMeaning: Tekrarlanan denemelerde bekleme süresini katlayarak artırma.
examples: Use **exponential backoff** for transient failures.
Adding jitter improves **exponential backoff**.

cards.definition: A mechanism that temporarily stops calls to a failing dependency.
cards.turkishMeaning: Arızalı bağımlılığa çağrıları geçici durduran mekanizma.
examples: The **circuit breaker** opened after repeated failures.
A **circuit breaker** gives the downstream service time to recover.

cards.definition: A limit on how long an operation may wait.
cards.turkishMeaning: İşlemin bekleyebileceği süre sınırı.
examples: Set a reasonable **timeout** for each request.
The database call exceeded its **timeout**.

cards.definition: A state where operations wait for each other and cannot proceed.
cards.turkishMeaning: İşlemlerin birbirini bekleyerek ilerleyemediği durum.
examples: The transaction ended in a **deadlock**.
Consistent lock ordering can prevent a **deadlock**.

cards.definition: A bug whose outcome depends on the timing of concurrent operations.
cards.turkishMeaning: Sonucu eşzamanlı işlemlerin zamanlamasına bağlı hata.
examples: The intermittent failure came from a **race condition**.
A lock protects this update from a **race condition**.

cards.definition: Memory that is no longer needed but is not released.
cards.turkishMeaning: Gereksiz hâle geldiği halde serbest bırakılmayan bellek.
examples: The **memory leak** caused gradual growth.
A profiler helped us locate the **memory leak**.

cards.definition: Automatic recovery of memory no longer used by a program.
cards.turkishMeaning: Programın kullanmadığı belleğin otomatik geri kazanımı.
examples: A long **garbage collection** pause increased latency.
The runtime handles **garbage collection**.

cards.definition: Keeping reusable results for faster future access.
cards.turkishMeaning: Sonuçları daha hızlı yeniden erişim için saklama.
examples: **Caching** reduced database traffic.
Incorrect **caching** can show outdated data.

cards.definition: Removing or marking cached data as no longer valid.
cards.turkishMeaning: Önbellekteki veriyi kaldırma veya geçersiz işaretleme.
examples: The bug was caused by missing **cache invalidation**.
Use an expiration policy for **cache invalidation**.

cards.definition: A model where copies become consistent after updates stop.
cards.turkishMeaning: Güncellemeler durunca kopyaların zamanla tutarlı olduğu model.
examples: The store provides **eventual consistency**.
With **eventual consistency**, a recent write may not appear immediately.

cards.definition: A group of operations treated as one logical unit.
cards.turkishMeaning: Tek mantıksal birim olarak ele alınan işlem grubu.
examples: The **transaction** updates both accounts.
Roll back the **transaction** if validation fails.

cards.definition: A controlled change to a database structure.
cards.turkishMeaning: Veritabanı yapısına kontrollü değişiklik.
examples: Test the **schema migration** on a copy of the data.
This **schema migration** adds a nullable column.

cards.definition: A data structure that makes certain lookups faster.
cards.turkishMeaning: Belirli aramaları hızlandıran veri yapısı.
examples: The query needs an **index** on the date column.
An **index** can add overhead to writes.

cards.definition: A request to retrieve or manipulate data.
cards.turkishMeaning: Veriyi alma veya değiştirme isteği.
examples: The **query** scans the whole table.
Optimize the **query** before adding more hardware.

cards.definition: Splitting data across multiple databases or machines.
cards.turkishMeaning: Veriyi birden fazla veritabanına veya makineye bölme.
examples: **Sharding** distributes the storage load.
Choose a good partition key before using **sharding**.

cards.definition: A system that holds messages until consumers process them.
cards.turkishMeaning: İletileri tüketiciler işleyene kadar tutan sistem.
examples: The worker reads from a **message queue**.
A **message queue** separates producers from consumers.

cards.definition: A queue holding messages that could not be processed successfully.
cards.turkishMeaning: İşlenemeyen iletileri tutan kuyruk.
examples: The failed message moved to the **dead-letter queue**.
Inspect the **dead-letter queue** before replaying messages.

cards.definition: A component that receives and processes messages or data.
cards.turkishMeaning: İleti veya veriyi alıp işleyen bileşen.
examples: The **consumer** acknowledges each message.
A slow **consumer** can increase the queue length.

cards.definition: A component that creates and sends messages or data.
cards.turkishMeaning: İleti veya veri üretip gönderen bileşen.
examples: The **producer** publishes an event after checkout.
Each **producer** must handle connection errors.

cards.definition: An HTTP notification sent automatically when an event occurs.
cards.turkishMeaning: Bir olay olduğunda otomatik gönderilen HTTP bildirimi.
examples: The **webhook** starts a build after a push.
Verify the signature of each **webhook**.

cards.definition: A setting that enables or disables a feature without a new deployment.
cards.turkishMeaning: Yeni dağıtım olmadan özelliği açıp kapatan ayar.
examples: The **feature flag** is off by default.
Use a **feature flag** for a gradual rollout.

cards.definition: A release exposed to a small group before wider deployment.
cards.turkishMeaning: Genel dağıtımdan önce küçük gruba sunulan sürüm.
examples: The **canary release** receives five percent of traffic.
Compare errors during the **canary release**.

cards.definition: Replacing instances gradually while others keep serving traffic.
cards.turkishMeaning: Diğer örnekler çalışırken örnekleri aşamalı değiştirme.
examples: The **rolling update** replaces one pod at a time.
Set readiness checks before a **rolling update**.

cards.definition: Releasing by switching traffic between two prepared environments.
cards.turkishMeaning: Trafiği hazır iki ortam arasında değiştirerek dağıtma.
examples: A **blue-green deployment** makes switching back easier.
Database changes complicate **blue-green deployment**.

cards.definition: A change that Git cannot combine automatically.
cards.turkishMeaning: Git'in otomatik birleştiremediği değişiklik çakışması.
examples: Resolve the **merge conflict** before merging.
Both branches edited the same line, causing a **merge conflict**.

cards.definition: Examining code changes before accepting them.
cards.turkishMeaning: Kod değişikliklerini kabulden önce inceleme.
examples: The **code review** caught an edge case.
Keep the **code review** focused on behavior and clarity.

cards.definition: An unusual input or condition near a boundary.
cards.turkishMeaning: Sınırda oluşan sıra dışı girdi veya durum.
examples: An empty list is an important **edge case**.
Add a test for this **edge case**.

cards.definition: A new change that breaks behavior that previously worked.
cards.turkishMeaning: Önceden çalışan davranışın yeni değişiklikle bozulması.
examples: The test caught a **regression** in search.
We reverted the change that caused the **regression**.

cards.definition: A test of a small, isolated piece of behavior.
cards.turkishMeaning: Küçük ve yalıtılmış davranışın testi.
examples: Write a **unit test** for the date calculation.
The **unit test** uses a fixed clock.

cards.definition: A test that checks how components work together.
cards.turkishMeaning: Bileşenlerin birlikte çalışmasını sınayan test.
examples: The **integration test** uses a temporary database.
An **integration test** caught the serialization mismatch.

cards.definition: A test that sometimes passes and sometimes fails without relevant changes.
cards.turkishMeaning: İlgili değişiklik olmadan bazen geçen bazen kalan test.
examples: The **flaky test** depends on network timing.
Fix the **flaky test** instead of ignoring all failures.

cards.definition: Future work created by shortcuts or aging technical choices.
cards.turkishMeaning: Kısayolların veya eski teknik tercihlerin yarattığı gelecek iş yükü.
examples: We reserved time to reduce **technical debt**.
This shortcut adds **technical debt**.

cards.definition: Changing code structure without intentionally changing behavior.
cards.turkishMeaning: Davranışı değiştirmeden kod yapısını düzenleme.
examples: The **refactoring** makes the parser easier to test.
Run the tests after **refactoring**.

cards.definition: An ordered list of work that has not been completed.
cards.turkishMeaning: Henüz tamamlanmamış işlerin sıralı listesi.
examples: Add the improvement to the **backlog**.
We reviewed the **backlog** before planning.

cards.definition: The agreed boundaries of a task or project.
cards.turkishMeaning: Görev veya projenin kararlaştırılmış kapsamı.
examples: This change is outside the current **scope**.
Clarify the **scope** before estimating.

cards.definition: An approximate calculation of effort, cost, or time.
cards.turkishMeaning: Emek, maliyet veya zaman için yaklaşık hesap.
examples: My **estimate** includes testing time.
The **estimate** may change after investigation.
cards.note: This card is the noun /ˈestɪmət/. The verb is /ˈestɪmeɪt/.

cards.definition: The latest agreed time for completing something.
cards.turkishMeaning: Bir işi tamamlamak için son tarih.
examples: We need to discuss the **deadline**.
The **deadline** is Friday afternoon.

cards.definition: A concrete result that must be provided.
cards.turkishMeaning: Teslim edilmesi gereken somut çıktı.
examples: The main **deliverable** is a working prototype.
Define each **deliverable** in the proposal.

cards.definition: A person or group affected by a project or decision.
cards.turkishMeaning: Proje veya karardan etkilenen kişi ya da grup.
examples: Invite a **stakeholder** from customer support.
Each **stakeholder** may have different priorities.

cards.definition: A specific task agreed during a discussion.
cards.turkishMeaning: Görüşmede kararlaştırılan belirli görev.
examples: Assign an owner to each **action item**.
The final **action item** is to update the documentation.

cards.definition: Transferring work or responsibility to another person.
cards.turkishMeaning: İşi veya sorumluluğu başkasına devretme.
examples: The shift **handoff** includes current incidents.
A clear **handoff** prevents missed tasks.

cards.definition: A request to agree on a shared understanding.
cards.turkishMeaning: … konusunda ortak anlayışa varabilir miyiz?
examples: **Could we align on** the priorities?
**Could we align on** the release criteria?

cards.definition: I will explain something step by step.
cards.turkishMeaning: Sana adım adım anlatayım.
examples: **Let me walk you through** the architecture.
**Let me walk you through** the deployment process.

cards.definition: A request for more detail about something.
cards.turkishMeaning: … konusunu biraz açabilir misiniz?
examples: **Could you elaborate on** the failure scenario?
**Could you elaborate on** your previous experience?

cards.definition: Used to raise a possible problem politely.
cards.turkishMeaning: … konusunda bir endişem var.
examples: **I have a concern about** the timeout setting.
**I have a concern about** exposing this endpoint.

cards.definition: Suggest discussing a detail separately after the meeting.
cards.turkishMeaning: Bunu toplantı dışında ayrıca konuşalım.
examples: **Let's take this offline** and compare the options.
**Let's take this offline** so the stand-up stays short.
cards.note: In meetings, offline means outside this discussion; it does not necessarily mean without the internet.

cards.definition: Thank you for drawing attention to this issue.
cards.turkishMeaning: Buna dikkat çektiğin için teşekkürler.
examples: **Thanks for flagging this**; I'll investigate.
**Thanks for flagging this** before the release.

cards.definition: We are working to understand a reported problem.
cards.turkishMeaning: Sorunu araştırıyoruz.
examples: **We are investigating** elevated error rates.
**We are investigating** and will update you in fifteen minutes.

cards.definition: The service is working again after a disruption.
cards.turkishMeaning: Hizmet yeniden çalışır durumda.
examples: **The service has recovered**, and we are monitoring it.
**The service has recovered** after the rollback.

cards.definition: A question asking how a good result will be measured.
cards.turkishMeaning: Başarılı sonuç nasıl görünecek; nasıl ölçülecek?
examples: **What would success look like** for this project?
**What would success look like** in my first three months?
